title: Composer - installing packages and using vendor/autoload.php
answer: Composer manages PHP packages. composer require adds a package and records it in composer.json and composer.lock. Every script then includes vendor/autoload.php once, and all installed classes load automatically. Commit composer.json and composer.lock, never the vendor folder.
pitfall: Running composer update on a live server can install untested new versions. Use composer install on servers, which reads the exact locked versions.

title: Manual autoloading with spl_autoload_register
answer: spl_autoload_register registers a function that PHP calls whenever an unknown class is needed. Convert the class name to a file path and require it. This is useful for tiny projects without Composer, but PSR-4 through Composer is the standard for anything larger.
pitfall: An autoloader that requires a missing file without checking file_exists first turns a typo into a fatal error with a confusing message. Check existence and let the next autoloader try.

title: PSR-4 autoloading - mapping namespaces to folders
answer: PSR-4 maps a namespace prefix to a folder, so App\Shop\Order loads from src/Shop/Order.php. Declare the mapping in composer.json, run composer dump-autoload, and never write manual require lines for your own classes again.
pitfall: PSR-4 is case-sensitive and the class name must match the file name exactly. A class called OrderService in a file named orderservice.php will not load on Linux.
